major_findings.title: Candidate retirement and output actions are not one ordered transition
major_findings.detail: Candidate A can close and unlock, candidate B can pause, and A can then send identifier-free continue that resumes B.
major_findings.required_decision: Serialize candidate claim and its local output action before another candidate starts.

major_findings.title: Joined timer callbacks can execute unbounded work
major_findings.detail: Commit actions include provider interruption, notification and channel publication that can block, so session finalization cannot safely join the whole callback.
major_findings.required_decision: Limit the joined callback to bounded local state and move blocking work to an independently owned lifetime.

major_findings.title: Reset-before-replay lacks implementation scope
major_findings.detail: Existing EOS interruption returns before reset completes, while the RFC does not authorize the EOS and TTS owner changes needed for a completion barrier.
major_findings.required_decision: Add explicit EOS and TTS reset ownership or remove held STT replay from the first implementation.

major_findings.title: Continuous STT callbacks lack immutable utterance attribution
major_findings.detail: A delayed result reads mutable current provider state and can be labeled as the next utterance even when packets contain a sequence field.
major_findings.required_decision: Implement provider-level immutable result attribution or disable transcript-based early commitment when provenance is unproved.

resolved_from_challenge_04: Direct text and word-trigger commits are explicit
Streamer-local output admission and notification-only public interruption are defined
next_action: Stop under the governed correction limit and obtain a maintainer decision between a VAD-only first release and broader STT, EOS and TTS ownership changes.
